_fixture: what .claude/skills/apply-job/scan-page.js produces for pages/ashby.html — GENERATED by running the real scanner over the served page, never hand-written
_bridge: tests/security/scan-fidelity.test.mjs runs the REAL scanner over that HTML and deep-compares this file to its output. Edit one and the other goes red.
_why: bench-apply.mjs's board resolver (fixtureScanPath) THROWS rather than measure a different page under this page's label, so `--board ashby` died with 'no scan fixture for board=ashby page=1' and Ashby — the board with the nonce CSP and the 700ms remount, i.e. the worst latency case the runner will meet — was unmeasurable. Phase 0.10.
_keys: COMBOS ARE STAMPED FIRST, as on greenhouse-step1: scan-page.js's combo loop runs before the input loop, so the location combobox is f1 and the text inputs start at f2, even though the sorted output puts the combo fifth. A fixture numbered in reading order is a shape the scanner cannot produce.
_sel: The combo has NO `sel`. stableSel() needs a unique id or a unique name/data-testid/data-qa/aria-label; this control has aria-labelledby (which stableSel does not read) and nothing else, exactly like Ashby's real react-select. So the filler must reach it positionally — which is precisely the handle the 700ms remount invalidates.
_v: The combo's `v` is its PLACEHOLDER text, 'Select a location'. It is not a value and nothing has been chosen; a consumer that treats a non-empty `v` as 'already answered' skips a required field on this board.
_remount: This is the PRE-remount DOM. ashby-step2.scan.json is the same form after the resume parse replaces the subtree ~700ms later.
